question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Storage-window degron: is AP-1 the memory, or just the writer?
ideas.description: Use dTAG/auxin degrons on endogenous FOS, JUN, JUNB and FOSL1 so that AP-1 can be eliminated selectively during the interval between a priming stimulus and a rechallenge, leaving induction and readout phases intact. If priming survives AP-1 loss during storage, AP-1 writes the memory into chromatin; if it collapses, AP-1 protein persistence is itself the memory trace, and the two cases are cleanly distinguished by a single timing variable.

ideas.title: Single-molecule footprinting of primed enhancers
ideas.description: Apply long-read methylation footprinting (Fiber-seq or SAMOSA) to naive, stimulated, and rested cells to ask whether primed AP-1 enhancers show a bimodal population in which a subset of molecules remain fully open and bound, versus a uniform intermediate state across all molecules. Population-average ATAC cannot tell these apart, yet they imply completely different memory mechanisms (a stable per-allele latch versus a graded relaxation).

ideas.title: Hysteresis mapping in stimulus dose space
ideas.description: Measure AP-1 target output across an ascending and then descending ladder of stimulus doses with matched equilibration times, testing for a hysteresis loop in which cells approaching from the high-dose side stay active at doses that cannot activate naive cells. An open loop is a direct, model-free signature of bistable memory, and the loop width quantifies memory depth; its absence argues for slow relaxation instead.

ideas.title: Mitosis-and-replication tracking of the primed state
ideas.description: Combine clonal barcoding with division counting (dye dilution or FUCCI-gated sorting) and single-cell multiome to measure how many cell divisions a primed AP-1 chromatin state survives, and whether sister cells inherit priming concordantly. Heritability across mitosis plus concordance between sisters is the operational definition of cellular memory and separates it from a long-lived but non-heritable cytoplasmic state.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 site arrays as a tunable memory element
ideas.description: Integrate at a fixed safe-harbor locus a panel of reporters whose enhancers differ in AP-1 site number, affinity, spacing and neighboring cofactor motifs, then run identical prime–wait–rechallenge protocols on each. This converts a correlational question into a design rule: it identifies the minimal cis architecture sufficient to store a transient AP-1 input and shows which features set memory duration.

candidates: Measure persistence of AP-1 motif-containing accessible chromatin peaks by ATAC-seq at a dense time course after a transient stimulus is withdrawn, relative to AP-1 protein decay kinetics
Acute auxin/dTAG degradation of FOS/JUN family members during the storage phase (after stimulus, before restimulation) to test whether continued AP-1 occupancy is required to maintain memory
Restimulation assay with graded doses and intervals to build a dose-response/decay curve of the primed response, giving a quantitative 'memory half-life' per gene
Single-cell lineage barcoding (e.g., Watermelon/CellTag) plus scATAC to ask whether primed accessibility and primed transcriptional output are heritable through mitosis within clones
Live-cell imaging of endogenous FOS/JUN translational-fusion reporters plus a downstream target reporter to correlate past AP-1 dynamics in individual cells with future response amplitude
Mitotic bookmarking test: live imaging and ChIP/CUT&RUN in synchronized mitotic cells to see whether AP-1 remains chromatin-bound on condensed chromosomes
Replication-coupled dilution test: label with EdU/SNAP-tag and ask whether primed enhancers survive S-phase and how many divisions memory survives
Synthetic AP-1 binding-site arrays with tunable number/affinity/spacing integrated at a safe harbor, to test what site architecture is sufficient to store a transient input
CUT&RUN/ChIP for individual AP-1 dimer partners over time to test whether memory corresponds to a handoff from early FOS-containing dimers to long-lived JUN/JUND/FOSL1 dimers
Targeted recruitment of AP-1 activation domains (dCas9-FOS/JUN) to naive loci without any stimulus, then withdrawal, to test sufficiency of AP-1 for establishing a persistent state
Hi-C/Micro-C or multiplexed DNA FISH before/after stimulus to test whether AP-1 creates persistent enhancer-promoter loops or compartment changes that outlast the signal
Quantify AP-1 protein and mRNA half-lives absolutely (SILAC pulse-chase, metabolic labeling) to determine whether slow turnover alone, rather than chromatin, explains apparent memory

Nucleosome-resolution MNase or long-read single-molecule footprinting (Fiber-seq/SAMOSA) to see whether primed enhancers retain open single-molecule footprints or just higher population-average accessibility
Test chromatin cofactor dependence of maintenance: inhibit/degrade p300, BRD4, BAF (SMARCA4), or H3K4me1 writers only during the storage window and score loss of priming
Combinatorial stimulus-identity test: prime with different AP-1-activating inputs and ask whether the stored state is input-specific or a generic AP-1 attractor, using matched ATAC/RNA signatures

Mathematical model comparison: fit bistable-feedback vs. slow-relaxation vs. chromatin-hysteresis models to time-course data and identify measurements that discriminate them (e.g., hysteresis loop in dose space)
Test AP-1 autoregulatory positive feedback directly by mutating AP-1 sites in the endogenous FOS/JUN/ATF3 promoters and measuring whether memory collapses

In vivo memory test: tamoxifen-inducible lineage labeling of AP-1-high cells (FOS-CreER) in wounded skin or inflamed tissue, then challenge weeks later and measure accelerated response in labeled progeny
Single-cell multiome in a prime-wait-rechallenge design to directly ask whether accessibility at AP-1 sites predicts which individual cells respond strongly to the second hit
Proteomic (RIME/BioID) comparison of AP-1 interactomes at naive vs. primed enhancers to identify the maintenance machinery that converts transient binding into a stable state
